beliefs.practice: Read the MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit it to source; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Use a secrets store for production credentials (Azure Key Vault or equivalent) and grant the application a least-privilege credential rather than embedding admin keys in config files.

Reuse a single MongoClient instance for the application lifetime (do not create a new client per request); configure connection pool parameters (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize) appropriate to expected concurrency.
Require TLS/SSL for all client connections and enforce secure socket options in the driver connection string and client config.
Enable and rely on driver retryable reads/writes where available and implement additional idempotent-safe retries with exponential backoff for transient network/timeout errors (with jitter).
Set reasonable serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS and connectTimeoutMS values to fail fast in startup and avoid hanging operations when the cluster is unreachable.

Perform heavy RFM aggregation work server-side with aggregation pipelines (use $group/$sum/$max/$count and $project) rather than pulling raw rows into the app; use allowDiskUse:true for large pipelines.
Use projection to limit returned fields in queries/aggregations to only what you need (especially when documents contain large arrays or embedded content).

Design documents to keep customer profile data in single documents when updates are frequent and sized reasonably; prefer embedding transaction summaries or references depending on query patterns and document size limits (avoid >16MB documents).

Create indexes on fields used for filtering and sorting in queries and aggregations (e.g., customerId, lastPurchaseDate, status) and use compound indexes for common combined filters to avoid collection scans.

For vector search, store embeddings in a consistent typed field (e.g., embedding: [float]) and create a vector index configured for your similarity metric (HNSW/IVF parameters tuned for dimension and recall), and keep the embedding dimension consistent across all documents.

If using cosine similarity, normalize vectors on insert (or index with appropriate index param) so that KNN using inner product returns cosine-ranked results; be explicit about normalization and metric used in the index settings.

Use metadata filters (standard indexed fields) in combination with $search/knn (or equivalent) to narrow candidate sets before KNN to reduce CPU and improve relevance (e.g., only match customers in same cohort or region).

When creating vector indexes, pick HNSW parameters (M, efConstruction) and query-time efSearch tuned for your data size and latency/recall tradeoff; test with explain/benchmarks and avoid default blindly.

Create indexes (including vector indexes) during maintenance windows or provision sufficient capacity temporarily; monitor for index build impact and prefer foreground/online build modes if supported to avoid long blocking operations.
Validate heavy queries with explain() and the cluster's query plan tools and examine index usage to ensure aggregations and $search/knn are using the intended indexes.
Use bulk writes / bulk upsert APIs for seeding or batch updates (e.g., when inserting computed embeddings or RFM values) to reduce round-trips and improve throughput.
Avoid multi-document transactions for high-throughput ingestion paths; prefer single-document updates or idempotent bulk operations unless strict cross-document atomicity is required.
Monitor cluster metrics (CPU, memory, index build progress, RU/IO consumption), enable slow query logging/profiling during tuning, and set alerts for increased latency or failed index builds.

Enable and verify backups and a tested restore procedure for the database that stores customer profiles and embeddings; ensure retention matches business requirements for data recovery and compliance.
Encrypt sensitive PII at rest and in transit; avoid storing cleartext sensitive identifiers in free-text LLM prompts or logs used for generating narratives unless redacted and consented.

When doing nearest-neighbor recall testing, build a reproducible benchmark dataset and measure both recall@k and latency for a range of efSearch/M settings rather than relying on single example queries.

Sharding: plan a shard key with high cardinality and even write distribution before scaling large collections (transactions across shards are more expensive); test query patterns with the chosen shard key.

Instrument the application to record what version of embeddings and what pipeline produced them (store embedding_version and timestamp) so re-computation and migration of vector indexes is auditable and reproducible.
Do not include production LLM or embedding API keys in runtime; gate LLM calls behind configuration and perform offline testing of narratives to avoid accidental data leakage to third-party LLMs.
